purpose: A depth-three clone of a ten-commit upstream. The three commits that came over were rewritten: the window's first commit has no parent at all, because there is nothing below the cut to point at, and `.git/shallow` names the tip. A history walker that walks to the root instead of to the shallow cut will ask for an object that is not in this repository and fail with a message nobody in the product can act on, so the corpus contains the shape and names the cut.

episodes.note: the shallow cut: a commit with no parent because the parent was never fetched

notes: the three visible commits are upstream rounds 6 to 8 with their ids intact, because a rewritten commit would no longer be a clone of anything; the boundary commit keeps a `parent` line pointing at round 5, which this repository does not contain, and `.git/shallow` names the boundary — that is exactly what `git clone --depth 3` leaves behind, and `git fsck --strict` agrees

findings.detail: the boundary commit's parent line names an object that was never fetched; the ingest must stop there and say so rather than fail
a shallow clone is not a corrupt one; fsck says so, and the fixture's own test says so
